source.title: On the Effectiveness of Lipschitz-Driven Rehearsal in Continual Learning
source.authors: Lorenzo Bonicelli; Matteo Boschini; A. Porrello; C. Spampinato; S. Calderara

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates Lipschitz regularization in continual learning and reports classification accuracy and measures related to buffer overfitting. This is a new setting and method relative to the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study does not test the listed claim versions directly. Its main tables compare continual-learning accuracy with and without LiDER; its buffer-guessing and perturbation analyses examine related properties. Reported gains cited from other work are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates Lipschitz regularization for rehearsal-based continual learning, not any listed version. Its weight-perturbation and Hessian analyses do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks. Buffer poisoning does not test V1's near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that LiDER mitigates replay-buffer overfitting by encouraging smoother decision boundaries and improves accuracy across the tested rehearsal methods and benchmarks. This does not establish any listed claim version.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds a learned Lipschitz regularization objective to rehearsal methods and evaluates continual-learning accuracy; it does not reproduce the listed random-label generalization experiments or their specified measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The benefit varies with rehearsal method and buffer size; authors report smaller benefit for GDumb with a reduced buffer. Applying LiDER to current-task examples gives inferior results to applying it to buffer examples. Hyperparameter sensitivity differs with pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: LiDER produces reported average accuracy gains of 2.32, 2.08, and 4.36 percentage points across the three benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding LiDER improves average continual-learning accuracy over the tested base methods under the reported tuning procedures.

fits_no_version.finding: LiDER has higher absolute accuracy at every reported poisoning level. It does not consistently reduce the loss relative to each method's unpoisoned accuracy: at p=.25%, losses are 8.40 points for DER++ and 8.47 for LiDER.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DER++ with LiDER retains higher absolute accuracy than DER++ across the tested replay-buffer poisoning levels.

fits_no_version.finding: Buffer-membership AUC decreases from .67 to .56, .58 to .50, and .55 to .54 with LiDER.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LiDER reduces score-based replay-buffer membership predictability in the tested ER-ACE settings, with the largest numerical reduction at the smallest buffer.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.3 reports improved weight-perturbation resilience and lower Hessian eigenvalue sums with LiDER; it does not report the train–test-gap ranking required by V7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-directed Lipschitz regularization also yields flatter parameter-space loss landscapes in the tested continual-learning models.

record.problems: The paper studies continual-learning accuracy and forgetting rather than the train-test error gap specified by the claim versions. Several robustness and weight-perturbation results are reported only in figures without textual numerical values; no uncertainty estimates are stated for the extracted results.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1, 2, and 4 report many separately paired benchmark, method, and buffer-size results; omitted because the study's LiDER continual-learning accuracy comparisons do not directly measure a listed claim version, and the authors additionally provide aggregate average gains in rows R1–R3. Figure 2's AUC entries are included for each buffer size. Other figure-only plots are not extracted because they do not test a listed version and lack descriptive numerical results.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The T3 assignment should be removed: a new setting qualifies only when its results bear on a listed version. All row states are cannot_determine relative to those versions; this does not dispute the reported method-performance gains.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness correlated with the train-test gap.
Removing the most memorized training examples and retraining.
